caption:
X Square's WALL-B robot sorted 1,816 parcels per hour in a recent one-hour livestream, achieving an accuracy rate above 98 percent.

For comparison, Figure Robot averaged 1,248 parcels per hour during a 200-hour test in May. X Square's throughput was approximately 45 percent higher.

Unlike humanoid systems, WALL-B uses two high-performance 6-axis robotic arms with specialized grippers. The system continuously adjusts its strategy as parcels move, overlap, or become obstructed.

After each pick, the robot reassesses the pile, adapting to changes such as deformed bags or misaligned labels. This minimizes the need for human intervention during exceptions.

The underlying AI model also applies in less predictable environments, such as household or tabletop tasks. This requires advanced perception and reasoning capabilities beyond repetitive routines.
